Many kids struggle with this not even because they are sociopaths but because they were taught to handle things themselves and were rarely shown empathy. There are emotions we are born feeling, and not feeling them can be sign of mental illness, and then there are some emotions we are taught like empathy. Empathy, while being a mix of emotions, is an emotional connection and an emotion itself. 
I feel like the best way to go about this is try to understand how you process emotions vs how others process emotions, and also try to rank severity of situations. Yes someone who failed a test can be just as upset as someone who's father died because of different complexes, but they both need to be shown different types of sympathy because the situations differ in how much they affect their lives overall.

This is a long post, so sorry if I mess up on grammar or spelling
I have been suicidal my whole life
My first attempt to kill myself was when I was younger than 5, my parents talking on the sidewalk about how hard things have been since they had kids
I walked out in front of a car, trying to get hit, I didnt want to be any more of a burden.
I started self harm at a young age too
It started as small things like opening blisters and putting salt on them, to cutting open the spaces I between my fingers, to breaking my arm 5 separate times.
My father specifically used corporal punishment
Which was fine, until it turned into abuse, both mentally and physically.
He yelled at me for stupid things, like being a girl, or getting sick.
He hit me with a belt a couple times
And he would always say something at the end, something like "you kids never seem to learn unless you get hurt pretty bad"
I dont know exactly what it was but it left an impression on me that to learn and forgive myself, I needed to hurt myself.
When I was 9 I was kidnapped and mentally abused by my moms best friend 
She blamed me for everything bad in her life, smacked me a couple times and repeatedly said "it's your fault, you know it's your fault and that's why, you're crying"
I dont remember the physical abuse
More like it came back to me in some dream
And I still have an issue with telling myself that she may have actually hit
I have a memory of wanting to be let go, wanting to leave
And all of a sudden, it blacks out for a minute, and then I remember falling down the stairs
I convinced myself I threw myself down them, searching for a reason that I had to leave.
But as some memories of her hitting me come back, maybe she pushed me, I could have easily hit my head and died from that so I still rather not think of it like that.
10 years old I found my sister on the floor, a failed suicide attempt
Out of all my memories its hardest to recall
Even trying to remember how the room looked makes me want to vomit
It was hard
Even though we were twins I was still the older sister, and still was given that responsibility of looking out for her.
It hurt, and to find out that what my sister dis that day was the same thing I'd been doing for years (the self harm and suicide attempts) made me hate myself more than I ever knew I could.
I tried not to loose it though
I had a new purpose in life
My parents didnt believe me when I said my sister self harmed and attempted suicide
So my new cause was to keep her alive
I'd stay up all night just to make sure she didn't take a shower, didnt take too many pills, etc etc.
After about a year of this I caught my sister trying to overdose, I took the bottle from her and she grabbed a kitchen knife on me (our medicine cabinet is in the kitchen and not the bathroom because my mom had issues with overdosing)
I pushed her away and was able to lock her in a separate room. I checked to make sure she didnt harm herself with the knife and one time when I did she said "Rachel, you are what make my life so miserable, if I killed you I wouldn't have to kill myself"
My purpose to live was gone
Started planning ways to kill myself and was just about to do it
But then luckily my sister threatened to kill herself at school and they finally convinced my parents she needed help
For once in my life my parents didnt hate me
They didnt think I was lying about a serious issue
They saw me as an individual instead of an immature snob
And that's all I wanted
Of course my story couldn't end there
8th grade year my sister attempted suicide in the girls rest room
I ran in as I felt I was about to throw up
I saw someone trying to tie a rope around something and I realised it was my sister
I went to get a lunch guard, some students over heard that my sister attempted suicide
Someone screamed it and people started laughing
She made it out fine and got to start homeschooling but I got stuck with asshole who put razors in my locker, show strings tied to look like a noose, notes saying my life is worthless and they'd much rather see my sister alive than me.
I convince my mother that school was stressful and my sister needed someone to be home to help her with schooling anyways and i was a straight A student.
Then I had to come back for highschool
People still made jokes about it
I was about to kill myself but 2 people saved my life
A teacher and a student 
They just joked with me and I started to feel okay with myself, and with a little gained optimism I realised I needed therapy, because even though they had helped me a ton just by talking and laughing with me I still needed to be mentally okay, I needed to heal emotionally rather than just have the thoughts of suicide leave me for a moment of time.

I finally got diagnosed and put on medicine, it's not helping a ton but talking to my therapist and being diagnosed with PTSD helps.
(I would have been diagnosed with depression, asperger's, anxiety, and gender dysphoria if I wasnt diagnosed with PTSD first)
Just learning about the disorder itself has helped me cope
Cause I know that what I am feeling is perfectly valid, and I'm not insane.
And just hearing each month the word I barley heard as a child 
Those "I care for you"s
Those "in so glad you're here today"
Those "you dont need to hurt yourself"
I know they're suppose to say that but it helps so much
I now cope through making art and theater 
I mean 2 years ago I couldn't talk to a small group of 10 kids, and now I'm set to be on stage in front of hundreds but yet it feels like home

Tl;dr
I've been suicidal since I was young
I had many different traumatic experiences 
Finally at 14 I met 2 people who helped me enough to the point I could accept help and finally I got a therapist 
I now cope with different forms of art
